title: SVG, sprites and texture atlases
summary: Load SVG artwork and reuse textures through atlases, subtextures and animated sprites.

blocks.text: SVG parses a complete SVG document into a hierarchy of vector entities, including supported transforms, styles, defs/use references and shapes. SVGPath provides a path-focused extraction route. SVG input is converted into engine geometry; it does not imply complete browser SVG/CSS feature support.

Use simple exported vector artwork first, then check nested transforms, inherited paint and holes against a visual reference. CSS filters, unsupported elements or external resources need explicit verification. Geometry equalization makes differently sampled contour sets compatible for morphing, but does not guarantee a visually meaningful correspondence.

TextureAtlas reads TexturePacker-style manifests in hash or array form. SubTexture stores normalized atlas coordinates with rotation and trimming metadata. Sprite draws a texture region; AnimatedSprite selects frames at a chosen cadence and looping mode. TextureManager owns shared texture aggregation and dirty flags.

cells: Fetch local or remote atlas data
Represent region, rotation and trimmed bounds
Sample the region in a compatible shader
Update frame selection in scene time
Upload/track shared textures and media changes

items: Keep atlas frame names and manifest paths consistent.
Account for trimmed logical size separately from stored pixel rectangles.
Verify cross-origin fetches and browser image decoding before diagnosing shader problems.
Preserve the emitting bundler’s asset URLs when serving a built package.
Set explicit output dimensions when comparing sprite images across different viewports.
